react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolomics dataset of ten metabolites yields a clear cross-paradigm consensus pointing to **galactose metabolism** as the dominant affected pathway. Across three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA (FDR = 7.5 × 10⁻¹⁵), MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA (p = 5.7 × 10⁻⁹), and mummichog m/z-network activity (p = 0.013) — the KEGG map hsa00052 / SMPDB SMP00043 pathway is the unanimous top-ranked hit. Five of the ten input metabolites map into this pathway via their curated member sets: **galactitol** (KEGG:C01697), **galactinol** (KEGG:C01235), **glycerol** (KEGG:C00116), **myo-inositol** (KEGG:C00137), and **sucrose** (KEGG:C00089). The shared structural theme is that all five are either galactose derivatives or inositol-derived galactosides, consistent with a blockade or shift in the Leloir pathway flux. A secondary convergence in ORA also captures **glycerophospholipid metabolism** (Reactome R-HSA-1483206, R-HSA-1483257; WikiPathways WP2533), driven by the same glycerol and myo-inositol hits, reflecting their dual role as membrane-phospholipid precursors. The three remaining input metabolites — pyrroline hydroxycarboxylic acid (C04281), detomidine (C07450), and phenylacetic acid (C07086) — did not resolve into the galactose cluster across any tool and appear as pathway orphans, suggesting they belong to distinct pharmacologically-driven or amino-acid-related perturbations uncaptured by the carbohydrate modules. Four driver metabolites — galactitol, galactinol, sucrose, and glycerol — are confirmed members of the Galactose Metabolism pathway (KEGG:map00052), with the first three directly implicated in the Leloir pathway enzymatic steps catalysed by GALK, GALT, and GALE, and glycerol acting as a downstream carbon-export form in this metabolic context.
